transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-27 14:30 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (CedarBridge), Liam (CedarBridge), Sofia (CedarBridge CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Quick review of tokens-per-dollar and tokens/sec tradeoffs; early wins from prefix caching; batching improved throughput but introduced tail latency.
- Action: share adjusted pricing + logs, run targeted 95th pct tests, confirm security contact and VPC details.

Topics: tokens/sec/$, caching savings, batching tradeoffs, dedicated vs hosted for pilot, SOC2/KMS questions

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick 40 min sync, run through the numbers from last week and then call out next steps
[00:12] Maya: yeah thanks, we only have like 40 minutes too so good pacing is helpful
[00:18] Priya: cool, i'll start with the metrics, so we ran the two configurations you asked: baseline hosted with no prefix caching, and the cached prefix config with batch window adjustments
[00:31] Priya: baseline we measured ~6k tokens per second at the cluster level, cost wise that mapped to about 120k tokens per dollar under the baseline run, uh which matched roughly earlier estimates
[00:45] Liam: wait 120k tokens per dollar, can you restate that, i thought we saw higher in the spreadsheet?
[00:51] Priya: yes so the spreadsheet of course mixes some assumptions — this is raw observed tokens/dollar during the test run with steady traffic, not the extrapolated monthly numbers. when we enable prefix cache we saw tokens/dollar improve to about 380k tokens per dollar for the same workload shape
[01:08] Sofia: that's a pretty big uplift, is that mostly caching or changes to quantization?
[01:13] Priya: mostly the prefix caching — so cold context repeats are avoided and the KV cache hit rate was around 57% in the run, though note the KV cache in our infra was spelled out as "K-V cash" in the logs earlier (laughs)
[01:26] Jordan: side note: there were a couple transcription typos in the auto exported logs which we cleaned but you'll see things like "K-V cash" and "batcher throttling" spelled oddly
[01:36] Maya: practical question — with caching on, we saw a latency bump for some requests though? some of our UX transactions are sensitive to p95 latency
[01:44] Priya: correct, when we turned up batching alongside caching to maximize tokens/sec the median latency stayed okay, around 120ms, but the 95th jumped from ~210ms to ~340ms in the worst config we tested
[01:58] Maya: ugh, 340ms p95 could be noticeable depending on the path. what was the batch window for that config?
[02:03] Priya: it was 200ms batch window, and the batching strategy used a 64-token target per batch, we also tried a 100ms window which reduced p95 back to ~260ms but dropped tokens/dollar about 15% from the cached-high config
[02:18] Liam: so tradeoff summary: caching gives you big cost savings but to get peak tokens/sec you need batching which increases tail latency. we care about both. is there a middle ground?
[02:27] Priya: yes, we're proposing an adaptive window: start at 80ms, increase to 150–200ms only when concurrency is above X (we use 40 concurrent requests as a heuristic). that got close to 300k tokens/dollar while keeping p95 generally under 280ms in our synthetic tests
[02:45] Jordan: another lever is model variant routing — run smaller quantized model for inference for background jobs and fall back to full model for high-fidelity requests. that gives a global percent cost reduction but adds complexity for you
[02:58] Sofia: we have the internal LLM team running a tiny q4 model — how hard is it to do model routing?
[03:04] Priya: it's supported by Redwood routing policies, we'd need to add a feature flag in your app or use the route key to decide. SE time to set that up is maybe a day for the pilot
[03:12] Maya: ok fairness question: are the tokens/dollar numbers normalized for the different GPUs? i.e. our dedicated capacity config had different hardware in the run vs hosted right?
[03:21] Priya: good catch — yes the dedicated run used A10p-like instance; the hosted was on mixed hardware. in the spreadsheet we normalized with effective vGPU hours and included infra cost assumptions; i'll attach both the raw logs and the normalized sheet
[03:33] Jordan: i'll share the adjusted price/throughput spreadsheet — it will show raw numbers and the normalized extrapolations for monthly usage patterns
[03:40] Liam: on security — we need confirmation for KMS integration and audit logs. our security lead wants to know retention window and whether logs contain PII; also SSO/SAML and RBAC mapping
[03:52] Jordan: for the pilot we can enable customer-managed KMS for private deployment, and we emit audit logs with request-id level entries. retention is configurable; enterprise options include longer retention for an add-on
[04:04] Sofia: and SOC2? we are getting pulled into that renewal window in July, will Redwood's SOC2 docs be enough?
[04:12] Jordan: Redwood has a SOC2 report we can share under NDA; we'll put that link in the follow up. also we can walk through the compliance checklist with your security team next week if you want
[04:22] Maya: great. also practical: the VPC peering attempt last week failed for us because of an egress firewall rule — Liam is going to follow up with infra to change it, but we may need a window to test again
[04:34] Liam: correct, i'll confirm the firewall rules and the peering window by end of week. i'll note that the private deployment path does add a little latency relative to hosted due to the peering but it's small if configured right
[04:45] Priya: back to perf — one other point: we ran a 10-minute stress test with burst patterns and saw cache cold-start cost hit. to mitigate we suggested a warm-up phase and a short-lived prefix prefetch for the top 5 routes which paid back in ~30 minutes of run time
[05:01] Maya: warm-up is fine, we can implement a short prefetch and maybe a tiny front-door cache in our app too to avoid cold misses
[05:09] Jordan: ok, let's outline next steps, i'll read them out and we can confirm
[05:13] Jordan: 1) Jordan sends adjusted pricing + normalized spreadsheet + raw perf logs (due Tue 3/2)
[05:20] Jordan: 2) Priya runs 95th pct latency canary with targeted batch window (due Thu 3/4)
[05:25] Jordan: 3) CedarBridge (Maya/Liam) to provide sample workload traces and confirm security contact for SOC2 scoping (due Wed 3/3)
[05:35] Sofia: that sounds good, one ask — can you also include a rough estimate for cost if we move to dedicated reserved capacity after pilot? maybe a ballpark for 3–6 month commit
[05:45] Jordan: yes i can add a reserved-capacity ballpark in the sheet; it'll include burst allowances and expected unit economics
[05:50] Maya: also, can we get the canary results instrumented to output a p95 per-route breakdown? that helps our front-end team decide which endpoints get extra optimization
[05:59] Priya: yes, we'll add per-route p95 and percentiles and a small post-run notebook that slices by prompt length and repeat rate
[06:08] Liam: okay cool, sounds like a plan. timing wise we'll aim to review next Tuesday if the logs and spreadsheet are in time
[06:15] Jordan: great, we'll target that. thanks everyone
[06:18] Sofia: thanks all
[06:20] Meeting end
